prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2024 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision
- Tackle the climate, cost-of-living and inequality crises together: invest boldly, follow science, and ensure a just transition that benefits everyone.
- Fund services by taxing wealth and pollution, end privatisation failures, and prioritise public and community ownership.

Health and care
- NHS: reverse privatisation; guarantee rapid GP access and universal NHS dentistry; restore public health budgets; invest £8bn extra in year one rising to £28bn by 2030, plus at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Primary care and dentistry: more GP time with patients, £2bn capital for primary care; NHS dentistry investment to £3bn/yr by 2030.
- Workforce: pay restoration (incl. junior doctors); school counsellors in every primary/secondary; mental health therapy within 28 days; National Cancer Plan.
- Social care: free personal care; rebuild workforce with national pay/career structures; invest £20bn/yr; £3bn more for children’s social care; improve support and benefits for disabled people and carers.

Homes and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/yr; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions.
- Retrofit and resilience: £29bn home insulation (to EPC B), £9bn low‑carbon heat, £7bn heat‑adaptation, £4bn for public buildings; Passivhaus-level new builds with solar and heat pumps; protect Green Belt; whole‑life carbon in planning.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax rising over a decade; accelerate renewables and storage, upgrade grid and interconnectors.
- Targets: wind to ~70% of electricity by 2030; by 2035 reach 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; end de‑facto ban on onshore wind; expand community energy and ownership.
- Oppose new nuclear; phase out existing stations; invest in green hydrogen and innovation; just transition with skills funding (£4bn/yr).

Economy and tax
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr (clean power, rail electrification, active travel, buildings, water/sewage).
- Public ownership of rail, water and Big 5 retail energy firms.
- Fair taxes: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn), align CGT and investment income with earnings, remove NI upper limit, fairer inheritance/property taxes; tougher windfall and avoidance measures; carbon tax to drive decarbonisation.
- Support SMEs via regional mutual banks, late-payment law, £2bn/yr local grants to decarbonise.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; protect 30% of land/sea by 2030; re‑wet peat; urban greening; ban destructive fishing; bring water into public ownership; +£1.5bn for DEFRA.
- Animal protection commission; ban blood sports, snares and lead ammo; end factory farming practices and routine antibiotics; reduce/replace animal testing.
- Food system: triple farm support for agroecology; expand UK horticulture; fair supply chains; free school meals for all and breakfast clubs to Year 6.

Education
- End tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; £8bn for schools plus £2.5bn/yr for buildings; £5bn for SEND; restore Sure Start (£1.4bn/yr); 35 hours funded childcare from 9 months; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; bring academies under local control; VAT on private school fees.

Transport
- Shift from roads to public transport and active travel: subsidies to £10bn/yr; £19bn over five years for upgrades; rail nationalisation; local control of buses; free bus travel for under‑18s; £2.5bn/yr for walking/cycling; oppose new roads; road pricing; end new ICE sales by 2027 and road use by 2035; fair EV transition; aviation frequent‑flyer levy, no airport expansion.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Fair Politics Act: scrap voter ID, adopt proportional representation, state party funding, lobbying/transparency reforms; replace Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; defend Human Rights Act; self‑ID for trans people; scrap anti‑protest laws.
- Migration: end hostile environment; safe routes; allow asylum seekers to work; abolish NRPF; simplify, humane system; fees at cost; NHS access.

Justice and policing
- Restore trust; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; invest to clear court backlogs; make misogyny a hate crime; fund services; decriminalise sex work.

Foreign policy
- Uphold international law; support Ukraine; EU re‑entry pathway (Customs Union, free movement, Erasmus).
- Gaza/Israel: immediate bilateral ceasefire; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; pursue war‑crimes accountability.
- Aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; Loss & Damage fund; debt relief; anti‑ISDS trade policy.
- Sign UN nuclear ban treaty; cancel Trident; pursue NATO reform and no‑first‑use.
